config.title: Form Validation with Zod + React Hook Form

intro.title: Form Validation with Zod + React Hook Form
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple user registration form that validates user input in real-time. You'll learn how to define validation rules using Zod, a TypeScript-first schema library, and integrate them with React Hook Form for efficient form state management. The core concept is using a schema to declare and enforce data shape and constraints, separating validation logic from your UI components. By the end, you'll have a form that displays clear error messages when invalid data is entered, using TypeScript for type safety throughout.
intro.usecase: Robust form validation is essential in any application that collects user input, from sign-up flows and checkout pages in e-commerce sites to data entry forms in admin dashboards. Using Zod with React Hook Form ensures data integrity and a smooth user experience by providing clear, real-time feedback on errors, such as invalid email formats or required fields left blank. This pattern is critical in production-grade software like customer relationship management (CRM) systems, financial platforms, and healthcare portals, where accurate data submission is non-negotiable. As a developer, mastering this combination allows you to build secure, maintainable forms that prevent invalid submissions and reduce backend errors.

objectives: Configure a React component with TypeScript to integrate React Hook Form and Zod
Initialize form state using React Hook Form's useForm hook with TypeScript types
Construct Zod schemas to define validation rules for form fields
Bind form inputs to React Hook Form's register function with proper TypeScript typing
Apply Zod schema validation to form data using React Hook Form's resolver
Manipulate form submission to handle validated data with TypeScript interfaces
Render validation error messages based on Zod schema violations
Control form reset behavior after successful validation and submission

steps.title: Import React, React Hook Form, and Zod
steps.instruction: Import React, useForm from 'react-hook-form', zod from 'zod', and zodResolver from '@hookform/resolvers/zod'.
steps.hint: Use import statements to bring in the necessary libraries for form validation.

steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary dependencies for form validation are imported.
successCriteria: React, useForm, zod, and zodResolver are imported correctly.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You imported some dependencies, but make sure to import React, useForm, zod, and zodResolver.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. Please import React, useForm from 'react-hook-form', zod from 'zod', and zodResolver from '@hookform/resolvers/zod'.

steps.title: Create the main Form component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Form that returns an empty fragment for now.
steps.hint: Define a component using either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. Return an empty fragment <> </>.
steps.seedCode:
// Import React, useForm from 'react-hook-form', zod from 'zod', and zodResolver from '@hookform/resolvers/zod'

// Create a functional component named Form that returns an empty fragment for now
steps.expectedOutcome: A Form component is defined and returns an empty fragment.
successCriteria: The Form component is defined and returns an empty fragment.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main Form component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a component named Form that returns an empty fragment.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Create a functional component named Form that returns an empty fragment.

steps.title: Define the Zod validation schema
steps.instruction: Inside your Form component, above the return statement, define a Zod schema named 'formSchema' that validates an object with two fields: 'name' (string, minimum 2 characters) and 'email' (valid email format).
steps.hint: Use z.object() to create the schema, then chain .min(2) on the name field and .email() on the email field.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Zod schema named 'formSchema' is defined with proper validation rules for name and email fields.
successCriteria: The schema is defined with z.object(), includes name field with .min(2) validation and email field with .email() validation.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that both fields have the correct validation methods: name should use .min(2) and email should use .email().
steps.feedbackWrong: The schema definition is missing or incorrect. Remember to use z.object() with the two required fields and their validation rules.

steps.title: Infer TypeScript type from Zod schema
steps.instruction: Inside your component, use Zod's `infer` to create a TypeScript type called `FormData` from your schema.
steps.hint: Use `z.infer<typeof schemaName>` to generate the type automatically from your Zod schema.
steps.expectedOutcome: A FormData type is created using z.infer<typeof yourSchema>.
successCriteria: The FormData type is correctly inferred from the Zod schema using z.infer.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using `z.infer<typeof yourSchema>` to generate the type.
steps.feedbackWrong: The FormData type wasn't created correctly. Use `z.infer<typeof yourSchema>` to infer the type from your Zod schema.

steps.title: Initialize React Hook Form with Zod resolver
steps.instruction: Inside your Form component, call the useForm hook with the zodResolver and your schema, specifying the FormData type as the generic parameter.
steps.hint: The useForm hook accepts a configuration object. Pass resolver: zodResolver(schema) and specify the generic type as FormData.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useForm hook is properly configured with the Zod resolver and the FormData type, enabling form validation.
successCriteria: useForm is called with the zodResolver(schema) and the FormData type is specified as the generic parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're passing the resolver configuration and specifying the FormData type.
steps.feedbackWrong: The form hook isn't properly set up. Review the useForm configuration for the resolver and type.

steps.title: Create the form structure
steps.instruction: Inside your Form component, return a <form> element with an onSubmit handler that calls the handleSubmit function from useForm.
steps.hint: The handleSubmit function is available from the useForm hook. Use it in the form's onSubmit attribute.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component returns a form element with an onSubmit handler wired to handleSubmit.
successCriteria: The form has an onSubmit attribute
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your form element has an onSubmit handler that calls handleSubmit.
steps.feedbackWrong: The form structure is missing or incorrect. Check that you're returning a <form> with an onSubmit handler.

steps.title: Add the name input field
steps.instruction: Inside your form, add a text input field for the name. Use the register function from useForm to connect it to React Hook Form.
steps.hint: Use the register function returned by useForm to register the input field. The input should have type='text' and a name attribute matching your schema field.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: registering an input field
<input type="text" {...register('fieldName')} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The form will contain a text input field for the name that is properly registered with React Hook Form.
successCriteria: The form contains an input element with type='text' that uses the register function from useForm.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an input field, but make sure you're using the register function from useForm to properly connect it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The name input field is missing or not properly connected to React Hook Form. Check that you're using the register function from useForm.

steps.title: Add the email input field
steps.instruction: Add an email input field to your form by updating the Zod schema to include an email field and adding a corresponding input element with the register function.
steps.hint: Update the schema object to include an email field with Zod validation, then add a new input element with type='email' and use register('email') to connect it to React Hook Form.
steps.expectedOutcome: The form will have two input fields: one for name and one for email, both connected to React Hook Form with proper TypeScript typing.
successCriteria: The Zod schema includes an email field with validation, and the form contains an email input element registered with useForm.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added both the email field to the Zod schema and the corresponding input element in the form.
steps.feedbackWrong: The email field isn't properly set up. Check that you've added it to the Zod schema and created an input element with type='email' and register('email').

steps.title: Add the submit button
steps.instruction: Inside the form, add a submit button element with the text 'Submit'.
steps.hint: Use a <button> element with type='submit' to create a form submission button.
steps.analogousExample:

<form>
  <input />
  <button type="submit">Submit</button>
</form>
steps.expectedOutcome: The form should now include a submit button that users can click to submit their input.
successCriteria: A <button> element with type='submit' and text 'Submit' is added inside the form.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has type='submit' and the text 'Submit'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The submit button is missing or incorrect. Add a <button type="submit">Submit</button> inside the form.

steps.title: Add form submission handler
steps.instruction: Create an onSubmit function inside your Form component that logs the validated form data when the form is submitted successfully.
steps.hint: Define a function that takes the form data as an argument and uses console.log to display it. Then pass this function to the handleSubmit method from react-hook-form.
steps.expectedOutcome: The form will have a submission handler that logs the validated data to the console when the form is submitted.
successCriteria: An onSubmit function is defined inside the Form component and passed to the handleSubmit method in the form's onSubmit attribute.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've defined a function that takes the form data as an argument and logs it, and that you're passing this function to handleSubmit in the form's onSubmit attribute.
steps.feedbackWrong: The submission handler isn't properly set up. You need to create a function that logs the form data and connect it to the form's submission.
